From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@orchard.health>

Cc: Matthew Price <matthew.price@orchard.health>

Subject: Post-demo notes + integration asks

Thanks again for the demo today — nice to see the low-latency extraction flows. Quick recap from our side and a few asks so we can scope an internal tech workshop: 

- Primary use case: structured extraction of discharge summaries and clinical notes into our EHR fields (SNOMED/LOINC mapping later). This needs structured output / tool-calling support to return JSON fragments we can map directly.
- Search & retrieval: we want embeddings for semantic candidate retrieval (patient similarity + historical notes), then a reranker to push the top 3 most-relevant notes.
- Latency targets: for interactive extraction calls we need p95 < 250ms for 200–400 token prompts. For batch/reranking jobs (overnight) throughput/cost matters more.
- Auth & security: Orchard stores PHI; we need guidance on Private (VPC) vs Dedicated with customer-managed KMS. SOC2 evidence and a short security questionnaire would help our procurement team.
- Region: must run in us-east for data residency.
- Cost: our finance team flagged a soft target of keeping inference cost for the extraction flows below $0.005 per extraction (ballpark).

Next steps we want from Redwood: short SDK quickstart for node/python with a structured-output example; a recommended routing/fallback policy (latency-first for extraction, cost-tiered fallback for overflow), and an initial plan for embeddings storage (regional) + reranker placement. Can you send those items and propose 60–90m workshop slots next week?

Attachments: [orchard_call_recording.mp3 (link)], [orchard_security_questionnaire.pdf]

Thanks,
Samira
Director of Clinical Integrations
Orchard Health

Hi Samira — great meeting, thank you. Short recap and action items from our side below. I pulled in Ben and Dev for the routing/auth specifics.

Recap / immediate recommendations:
- SDK quickstart: attaching a focused quickstart (node + python) showing structured output / tool-calling. See attached redwood_sdk_quickstart.pdf.
- Routing policy (proposal):
  * Extraction route: latency-first policy on dedicated us-east pool (p95 target 250ms). Primary model: rw-infer-13b-llama-q8 (low-latency quantized variant).
  * Fallback chain: if latency SLO at pool is missed or capacity constrained -> fallback to rw-infer-7b-quant (slightly cheaper, slightly lower quality) -> final fallback to hosted low-cost scalar (best-effort, higher latency but cheaper).
  * Reranker flow: candidate generation using embeddings on a dedicated embedding pool (us-east), then pass top-N (N=20) to a reranker model hosted in the same region for minimal cross-region latency.
- Embedding storage: recommend regional vector DB (us-east); we can provide recommended TTL/refresh cadence and sharding hints after workshop.
- Auth & security: will send the SOC2 summary and the security questionnaire (attached). For PHI we recommend Private (VPC) deployment or Dedicated with customer-managed KMS depending on procurement timeline.

Action items (we will deliver):
1) Send SDK quickstart + example structured-output prompt and response (attached).
2) Draft YAML for proposed routing policy (attached: proposed-routing-policy.yaml).
3) Provide SOC2 evidence + completed questionnaire (attached orchard_security_questionnaire.pdf).
4) Schedule a technical workshop (60–90m) with Ben (solutions), Dev (runtime engineer), and your infra/security lead.

Proposed workshop slots: Tue 2026-06-16 10:00–11:30 PT, Wed 2026-06-17 13:00–14:30 PT. Let us know which works.

Attachment stubs: [redwood_sdk_quickstart.pdf], [proposed-routing-policy.yaml], [orchard_security_questionnaire.pdf]

Subject: FW: Orchard Health — routing details & recommended model families

Kimberly / Dev — forwarding a few notes after reviewing the call transcript and Samira's latency/cost targets. A couple of engineering clarifications we should confirm on the workshop: 

- Model families: recommend starting with rw-infer-13b-llama-q8 for extraction (quantized 8-bit kernels on A100/A10), and rw-infer-7b-quant as the primary fallback. For reranker consider a specialized cross-encoder 2–4B family that balances relevance and cost.
- KV cache / prefix caching: for repeated patient-context prompts, enable short-term KV caching (TTL ~2m) to avoid re-computing attention for follow-up interactions — huge p95 improvement. We should demonstrate cache hit metrics in the workshop.
- Auth: for PHI we should propose two deployment options in the PO (procurement):
  1) Private (VPC) with customer-managed KMS + HSM integration (preferred if procurement allows).
  2) Dedicated with enforced network isolation and CMEK (customer-managed encryption keys).
- SDK wiring sample (inline suggestion):
  * node: set routingPolicy: {primaryPool: "us-east-latency-dedicated", fallbackChain: ["us-east-cost-7b", "hosted-scalar"] }
  * auth: recommend mTLS for service-to-service calls and short-lived tokens for client calls.

Cost note: rough estimate for interactive extraction path (rw-infer-13b-llama-q8) ~ $0.0045–$0.006 per extraction depending on prompt size and batching; we'll refine after we map typical token sizes.

I'll prep a short deck with model-family tradeoffs and a sample routing-policy YAML to walk through at the workshop.

- Ben
Solutions Engineering
